text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah, hiya. Yeah, I can hear you.
A: Good. I'm Abena.
B: Dean. Nice to meet you.
A: And you. So. Where are you?
B: Tipton. Black Country. Near Dudley, sort of.
A: I know the name. I'm in Thornton Heath, in Croydon. South London.
B: Ar, right. Never been down that way much. Only Palace for the football, once.
A: What do you do for work, Dean?
B: Er, press operator. Metal pressings, in Wednesbury. You put the sheet in, it stamps it, brackets and that for cars. Days and lates.
A: Do you like it?
B: Yeah. It's alright. It's steady, you know. Lads are sound. I don't get stressed with it.
A: That's worth something. I'm a practice administrator at a GP surgery in Norbury. Part-time, mornings, Monday to Thursday.
B: Oh right. My missus works in a care home. She's always on about trying to get through to the GP on the phone.
A: Eight o'clock. Everybody rings at eight o'clock, and then they're cross with the receptionist because there are only so many appointments. It's not the receptionist's fault, you know. I tell people that very plainly.
B: [laughs] Yeah, I bet you do.
A: I do. Erm, I do the rota and the letters, referrals, that kind of thing. Somebody has to know where everything is.
B: Ar. Kayleigh does all that at ours. Bills, forms. I'd lose 'em.
A: You would lose them?
B: Yeah, honestly. Ruby's school sent another letter home this week, trip form, and I forgot to sign it. Again. It's still in me coat, I think.
A: How old is Ruby?
B: Eight. She's Kayleigh's, but... she's mine, sort of, do you know what I mean.
A: Yes. Well, sign the form tonight. Put it by the kettle. That's what I'd do.
B: [laughs] By the kettle. Yeah, that's a good shout.
A: My son is twenty, at university in Leicester. He only rings when he needs money. So the forms never end, they just change.
B: [laughs] Ar.
A: What do you do at the weekend?
B: Weekend... er, fishing mostly. On the canal, or there's a pool near Himley. Caught a decent carp last Sunday. Fourteen pound, about.
A: Is that big?
B: For there, yeah. I put it back, though.
A: You put it back? After all that.
B: Yeah, you're meant to. It's just the sitting there, really. Nobody bothering you.
A: I understand that. I walk, Norwood Grove most days. And I have tomatoes in the garden. They're doing very well this year. Kwame, my husband, says I talk to them.
B: Do you?
A: Not out loud. ...Sometimes.
B: [laughs]
A: And then Sunday is church. I sing in the choir.
B: Sunday's my mum's, for us. Big dinner in Great Bridge, whole family.
A: What does she cook?
B: Roast. Beef usually, Yorkshires. Same every week.
A: Every week the same?
B: Yeah. I'm not, er, adventurous with food.
A: No? Then I would give you light soup and fufu.
B: Is it spicy?
A: It can be.
B: I don't go past a korma, me.
A: Then we would start you gently.
